features: A BUILDING READY MADE, TO SEE AT ONCE WHAT THE PROGRAM DOES — ⚠️ This version touches the database: one migration adds a column to buildings to mark the demonstration one. It changes no existing building.

THE PROBLEM: whoever installs KondoManager faces an empty program, and an empty program shows nothing. To see it working you had to enter units, people, thousandths, budget and instalment plan by hand — an hour's work before you could judge whether the software suits you.

THE CREATION PAGE NOW HAS A BUTTON that builds a complete building with realistic data: four units with owners, a tenant and two co-owners; the millesimal tables, including the roof terrace split under article 1126 of the Italian civil code — one third to whoever has exclusive use, two thirds to everyone else, on two tables linked to the same cost; the budget, one item of which is split between owner and tenant; the instalment plan generated by the real engine; two payments in, one of them partial, leaving arrears to look at; a supplier invoice with withholding tax and a credit note offset against it, so that less leaves the bank than the debt closed; and a transfer feeding the works fund.

IT CAN BE REMOVED, AND THAT IS THE HALF THAT MATTERS. A building with accounting movements normally cannot be deleted — a deliberate protection: bookkeeping must not vanish at the press of a button. The demonstration building is the only exception, for a precise reason: those movements were written by the program, not by a building manager. Removal asks for confirmation and says what it is about to delete.
ONE AT A TIME: when a demonstration building already exists the button switches off, and in its place appear the links to open it and to remove it.

AND THE ERROR MESSAGE ON REAL BUILDINGS NOW SAYS WHY. Trying to delete a building with accounting movements showed only «an error occurred during deletion»: you could not tell whether it was a fault or a rule, nor that retrying was pointless. The message now says that the building has payments, F24 forms or cash accounts on record and that this is why it cannot be deleted, because deleting it would throw away its bookkeeping.

UNDER THE BONNET, THE CHOICE THAT MAKES THIS WORK LAST: the demonstration building is not written straight into the database but built through the same doors a building manager uses — the invoice service, the payment service, the instalment plan generator, the receipt, the transfer. That means it cannot produce situations the program cannot produce, and it updates itself when the program changes. Building it this way surfaced three points where writing by hand would have produced a fake building: an expense item without its accounting anchor cannot be invoiced, the invoice service requires the payment method, and an instalment plan must declare which items it covers — without that the dashboard reports it as misaligned and the demo would open with a red alert. Eight automated checks now require the building to be constructed without a single warning, the dashboard to find it aligned, the removal to leave nothing behind, and that removal to refuse to touch a real building.
